To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The Bayesian analysis pipeline for testing General Relativity using gravitational waves signals from binary neutron stars is capable of detecting the presence of spins and of constraining their magnitudes, even when the spin-induced effects are small.

the Bayesian analysis pipeline can be used to test the validity of GR using the signals from coalescences of neutron stars with spins, but that the accuracy with which the parameters of the source can be measured is degraded by the presence of spin.

(1) the Bayesian evidence for the presence of a neutron star binary with spins in the data can be used to test GR; (2) the posterior probability distributions of the spin parameters can be used to constrain the spins; (3) the posterior probability distribution of the chirp mass can be used to infer the mass of the source; (4) the posterior probability for GR is not affected by the inclusion of spins in the analysis;

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the sources we considered here, the Bayesian data analysis pipeline is capable of detecting the effects of spins, and of distinguishing between GR and alternative theories of gravity.
, if the sources have spins, the Bayesian analysis is more powerful than the Fisher matrix analysis.

the current state of the art in gravitational wave data analysis, when combined with the current state of knowledge of the neutron star equation of state, does not provide a conclusive statement on the validity of general relativity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Bayesian analysis pipeline is robust and can be used for the detection of gravitational waves from binary compact objects.
, the Bayesian data analysis pipeline can be used to test GR with binary neutron stars with spin effects included.
the Bayesian analysis pipeline performs well in the presence of spins and that the constraints on the deviation from GR can be further improved by including spins in the analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current data is not yet sensitive enough to constrain the dimensionless spin magnitudes of the binary neutron star sources.
the inclusion of spin effects does not affect significantly the performance of the pipeline, which is able to test GR with a high degree of confidence even in the presence of spins.
, even with spins taken into account, the pipeline is capable of testing GR using gravitational waves from coalescing binary neutron stars.
